newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Applied Materials to acquire Opal, Orbot.
newsitem.headline: Applied Materials to acquire Opal, Orbot.

text.p: Applied Materials Inc's agreement to acquire Opal Inc and Orbot Instruments Ltd for a total of approximately $285 million has been hailed as the biggest deal of its kind in Israel's high tech sector.

"This is the largest M&A transaction in the history of high tech in Israel...It's certainly a noteworthy event," Dennis Hunter, Applied Materials managing director, corporate development, told a Tel Aviv news conference.

California-based Applied Materials is the leading maker of equipment used to produce computer chips. Hunter said the acquisitions were in line with the company's goal to become a leader in the metrology and inspection markets.

Applied Materials will buy Opal, a leading supplier of semiconductor test equipment, for about $175 million and Orbot, a privately owned supplier of wafer inspection systems, for about $110 million in cash.

"What the core is in this business is pattern recognition, optics and artificial intelligence. These are things in which we are not experienced. These are things in which Israel has a superb tradition of excellence," Hunter said.
Orbot's board of directors has approved the sale.

Major shareholders in Orbot are Ormat Industries Ltd, a leading industrial holding company, and Carroll Acquisition Corp, owned by U.S. businessman William Davidson. Together they hold about 16 percent of Orbot's shares, said Zvi Lapidot, Orbot chairman.
Applied Materials said it expected to commence a cash tender offer on or before November 27 for Opal at $18.50 per share.
Israel's Clal Electronics Industries, a subsidiary of Clal Industries, said it would receive $50 million for the sale of its approximately 30 percent stake in Opal.
Applied said it had signed an agreement in which Orbotech Ltd will sell its 14 percent stake in Opal.
Applied said additional shareholders of Opal, whose holdings together with those of Orbotech and Clal constitute about 49 percent of Opal's share capital, have signed similar agreements.
Orbotech makes automated optical inspection systems for use in the manufacture of printed circuit boards.

Both transactions are expected to be completed during Applied Materials' first fiscal quarter ending January 26, 1997. The company said it expected the acquisitions would result in a first-quarter fiscal 1997 pre-tax charge for acquired in-process research and development in the range of $50 million-$60 million, or $0.27 to $0.32 a share after tax.
Opal's revenues for the 12 months ended September 30, 1996, were $62 million. For the fiscal year ended December 31, 1995, they were $45 million. Opal employs some 325 people.
Orbot's revenues for the same periods were, in 1996, $36 million, and in 1995, $19 million. It has some 200 employees.
Hunter said the two operations combined could within six to seven years hit "the billion dollars" mark.
"A typical applied billion dollar division has got about 1,000 to 1,200 people in it," Hunter said. "There are already plans underway for the expansion of Opal or the building of a new facility."
